17771.label: Isaiah 1:1
17771.text: The vision that Isaiah the son of Aʹmoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uz·ziʹah, Joʹtham, Aʹhaz, and Hez·e·kiʹah, kings of Judah:

17772.label: Isaiah 1:2
17772.text: Hear, O heavens, and pay attention, O earth, For Jehovah has spoken: “Sons I have brought up and raised, But they have revolted against me.

17773.label: Isaiah 1:3
17773.text: A bull well knows its buyer,And a donkey the manger of its owner;But Israel does not know me, My own people do not behave with understanding.”

17774.label: Isaiah 1:4
17774.text: Woe to the sinful nation, The people weighed down with error,A brood of wicked men, corrupt children! They have abandoned Jehovah; They have treated the Holy One of Israel with disrespect;They have turned their backs on him.

17775.label: Isaiah 1:5
17775.text: Where will you be struck next as you add to your rebellion? The whole head is sick,And the whole heart is diseased.

17776.label: Isaiah 1:6
17776.text: From the sole of the foot to the head, nothing is healthy. There are wounds and bruises and open sores—They have not been treated or bound up or softened with oil.

17777.label: Isaiah 1:7
17777.text: Your land is desolate. Your cities are burned with fire. Foreigners devour your land right in front of you. It is like a wasteland overthrown by foreigners.

17778.label: Isaiah 1:8
17778.text: The daughter of Zion has been left like a shelter in a vineyard,Like a hut in a cucumber field,Like a city under siege.

17779.label: Isaiah 1:9
17779.text: Unless Jehovah of armies had left us a few survivors,We should have become just like Sodʹom,And we should have resembled Go·morʹrah.

17780.label: Isaiah 1:10
17780.text: Hear the word of Jehovah, you dictators of Sodʹom. Pay attention to the law of our God, you people of Go·morʹrah.

17781.label: Isaiah 1:11
17781.text: “Of what benefit to me are your many sacrifices?” says Jehovah. “I have had enough of your burnt offerings of rams and the fat of well-fed animals, And I have no delight in the blood of young bulls and lambs and goats.

17782.label: Isaiah 1:12
17782.text: When you come to appear before me, Who has required this from you,This trampling of my courtyards?

17783.label: Isaiah 1:13
17783.text: Stop bringing in any more worthless grain offerings. Your incense is detestable to me. New moons, sabbaths, the calling of conventions —I cannot put up with the use of magical power along with your solemn assembly.

17784.label: Isaiah 1:14
17784.text: I have hated your new moons and your festivals. They have become a burden to me;I am tired of bearing them.

17785.label: Isaiah 1:15
17785.text: And when you spread out your palms,I hide my eyes from you. Although you offer many prayers, I am not listening; Your hands are filled with blood.

17786.label: Isaiah 1:16
17786.text: Wash yourselves, make yourselves clean; Remove your evil deeds from my sight;Stop doing bad.

17787.label: Isaiah 1:17
17787.text: Learn to do good, seek justice, Correct the oppressor,Defend the rights of the fatherless child, And plead the cause of the widow.”

17788.label: Isaiah 1:18
17788.text: “Come, now, and let us set matters straight between us,” says Jehovah. “Though your sins are like scarlet,They will be made as white as snow; Though they are as red as crimson cloth,They will become like wool.

17789.label: Isaiah 1:19
17789.text: If you show willingness and listen,You will eat the good things of the land.

17790.label: Isaiah 1:20
17790.text: But if you refuse and rebel,You will be devoured by the sword, For the mouth of Jehovah has spoken it.”

17791.label: Isaiah 1:21
17791.text: How the faithful city has become a prostitute! She was full of justice; Righteousness used to lodge in her, But now murderers.

17792.label: Isaiah 1:22
17792.text: Your silver has become dross, And your beer is diluted with water.

17793.label: Isaiah 1:23
17793.text: Your princes are stubborn and partners with thieves. Every one of them loves a bribe and chases after gifts. They do not grant justice to the fatherless, And the legal case of the widow never reaches them.

17794.label: Isaiah 1:24
17794.text: Therefore the true Lord, Jehovah of armies,The Powerful One of Israel, declares: “Ah! I will rid myself of my adversaries,And I will take revenge on my enemies.

17795.label: Isaiah 1:25
17795.text: I will turn my hand against you,I will smelt away your dross as with lye,And I will remove all your impurities.

17796.label: Isaiah 1:26
17796.text: I will restore your judges as in the beginningAnd your advisers as at the start. After this you will be called City of Righteousness, Faithful Town.

17797.label: Isaiah 1:27
17797.text: With justice Zion will be redeemed, And her people who return, with righteousness.

17798.label: Isaiah 1:28
17798.text: The rebels and the sinners will be broken together, And those leaving Jehovah will come to their finish.

17799.label: Isaiah 1:29
17799.text: For they will be ashamed of the mighty trees that you desired, And you will be disgraced because of the gardens that you chose.

17800.label: Isaiah 1:30
17800.text: For you will become like a big tree with withering leaves, And like a garden without water.

17801.label: Isaiah 1:31
17801.text: The strong man will become tow, And his work a spark;Both of them will go up in flames together,With no one to extinguish them.”

17802.label: Isaiah 2:1
17802.text: This is what Isaiah the son of Aʹmoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem:

17803.label: Isaiah 2:2
17803.text: In the final part of the days, The mountain of the house of JehovahWill become firmly established above the top of the mountains, And it will be raised up above the hills,And to it all the nations will stream.

17804.label: Isaiah 2:3
17804.text: And many peoples will go and say: “Come, let us go up to the mountain of Jehovah,To the house of the God of Jacob. He will instruct us about his ways,And we will walk in his paths.” For law will go out of Zion,And the word of Jehovah out of Jerusalem.

17805.label: Isaiah 2:4
17805.text: He will render judgment among the nationsAnd set matters straight respecting many peoples. They will beat their swords into plowsharesAnd their spears into pruning shears. Nation will not lift up sword against nation,Nor will they learn war anymore.

17806.label: Isaiah 2:5
17806.text: O house of Jacob, come,Let us walk in the light of Jehovah.

17807.label: Isaiah 2:6
17807.text: For you have forsaken your people, the house of Jacob, Because they have become full of things from the East;They practice magic like the Phi·lisʹtines,And they abound with the children of foreigners.

17808.label: Isaiah 2:7
17808.text: Their land is filled with silver and gold,And there is no limit to their treasures. Their land is filled with horses,And there is no limit to their chariots.

17809.label: Isaiah 2:8
17809.text: Their land is filled with worthless gods. They bow down to the work of their own hands,To what their own fingers have made.

17810.label: Isaiah 2:9
17810.text: So man bows down, he becomes low,And you cannot possibly pardon them.

17811.label: Isaiah 2:10
17811.text: Enter into the rock and hide yourself in the dustBecause of the terrifying presence of JehovahAnd his majestic splendor.

17812.label: Isaiah 2:11
17812.text: The haughty eyes of man will be brought low,And the arrogance of men will bow down. Jehovah alone will be exalted in that day.

17813.label: Isaiah 2:12
17813.text: For it is the day belonging to Jehovah of armies. It is coming upon everyone who is haughty and lofty,Upon everyone, whether exalted or lowly,

17814.label: Isaiah 2:13
17814.text: Upon all the cedars of Lebʹa·non that are lofty and exaltedAnd upon all the oaks of Baʹshan,

17815.label: Isaiah 2:14
17815.text: Upon all the lofty mountainsAnd upon all the high hills,

17816.label: Isaiah 2:15
17816.text: Upon every high tower and every fortified wall,

17817.label: Isaiah 2:16
17817.text: Upon all the ships of Tarʹshish And upon all desirable boats.

17818.label: Isaiah 2:17
17818.text: Man’s haughtiness will be brought down,And the arrogance of men will bow low. Jehovah alone will be exalted in that day.

17819.label: Isaiah 2:18
17819.text: The worthless gods will completely disappear.

17820.label: Isaiah 2:19
17820.text: And people will enter into the caves of the rocksAnd into the holes in the ground, Because of the terrifying presence of JehovahAnd his majestic splendor, When he arises to make the earth tremble in terror.

17821.label: Isaiah 2:20
17821.text: In that day men will take their worthless gods of silver and of goldThat they had made for themselves to bow down toAnd throw them away to the shrewmice and to the bats,

17822.label: Isaiah 2:21
17822.text: In order to enter into the holes in the rocksAnd into the clefts of the crags,Because of the terrifying presence of JehovahAnd his majestic splendor,When he arises to make the earth tremble in terror.

17823.label: Isaiah 2:22
17823.text: For your own sakes, quit trusting in mere man,Who is only the breath in his nostrils. Why should he be taken into account?

17824.label: Isaiah 3:1
17824.text: For look! the true Lord, Jehovah of armies,Is removing from Jerusalem and Judah every kind of support and supply,All support of bread and water,

17825.label: Isaiah 3:2
17825.text: Mighty man and warrior,Judge and prophet, diviner and elder,

17826.label: Isaiah 3:3
17826.text: Chief of 50, dignitary, and adviser,The expert magician and the skilled charmer.

17827.label: Isaiah 3:4
17827.text: I will make boys their princes,And the unstable will rule over them.

17828.label: Isaiah 3:5
17828.text: The people will oppress one another,Each one his fellow man. The boy will assault the old man,And the lightly esteemed one will defy the respected one.

17829.label: Isaiah 3:6
17829.text: Each one will take hold of his brother in his father’s house and say: “You have a cloak—you be our commander. Take charge of this overthrown pile of ruins.”

17830.label: Isaiah 3:7
17830.text: But he will protest in that day: “I will not be your wound dresser; I have no food or clothing in my house. Do not make me commander over the people.”

17831.label: Isaiah 3:8
17831.text: For Jerusalem has stumbled,And Judah has fallen,Because in word and deed they are against Jehovah;They behave defiantly in his glorious presence.

17832.label: Isaiah 3:9
17832.text: The expression of their faces testifies against them,And they proclaim their sin like Sodʹom; They do not try to hide it. Woe to them, for they are bringing disaster on themselves!

17833.label: Isaiah 3:10
17833.text: Tell the righteous that it will go well for them;They will be rewarded for what they do.

17834.label: Isaiah 3:11
17834.text: Woe to the wicked one! Disaster will befall him,For what his hands have done will be done to him!

17835.label: Isaiah 3:12
17835.text: As for my people, their taskmasters are abusive,And women rule over them. My people, your leaders are causing you to wander,And they confuse the direction of your paths.

17836.label: Isaiah 3:13
17836.text: Jehovah is taking his position to accuse;He is standing up to pass sentence on peoples.

17837.label: Isaiah 3:14
17837.text: Jehovah will enter into judgment with the elders and princes of his people. “You have burned down the vineyard,And what you have stolen from the poor is in your houses.

17838.label: Isaiah 3:15
17838.text: How dare you crush my peopleAnd grind the faces of the poor in the dirt?” declares the Sovereign Lord, Jehovah of armies.

17839.label: Isaiah 3:16
17839.text: Jehovah says: “Because the daughters of Zion are haughty,Walking with their heads high, Flirting with their eyes, skipping along,Making a tinkling sound with their anklets,

17840.label: Isaiah 3:17
17840.text: Jehovah will also strike the head of the daughters of Zion with scabs,And Jehovah will make their forehead bare.

17841.label: Isaiah 3:18
17841.text: In that day Jehovah will take away the beauty of their bangles,The headbands and the crescent-shaped ornaments,

17842.label: Isaiah 3:19
17842.text: The earrings, the bracelets, and the veils,

17843.label: Isaiah 3:20
17843.text: The headdresses, the ankle chains, and the breastbands, The perfume receptacles and the charms,

17844.label: Isaiah 3:21
17844.text: The finger rings and the nose rings,

17845.label: Isaiah 3:22
17845.text: The ceremonial robes, the overtunics, the cloaks, and the purses,

17846.label: Isaiah 3:23
17846.text: The hand mirrors and the linen garments, The turbans and the veils.

17847.label: Isaiah 3:24
17847.text: Instead of balsam oil, there will be a rotten smell;Instead of a belt, a rope;Instead of a beautiful hairstyle, baldness; Instead of a rich garment, a garment of sackcloth; And a brand mark instead of beauty.

17848.label: Isaiah 3:25
17848.text: By the sword your men will fall,And your mighty men in battle.

17849.label: Isaiah 3:26
17849.text: Her entrances will mourn and grieve, And she will sit on the ground desolate.”

17850.label: Isaiah 4:1
17850.text: And seven women will grab hold of one man in that day, saying: “We will eat our own breadAnd wear our own clothing;Only let us be called by your nameTo take away our disgrace.”

17851.label: Isaiah 4:2
17851.text: In that day what Jehovah makes sprout will be splendid and glorious, and the fruitage of the land will be the pride and beauty of the survivors of Israel.

17852.label: Isaiah 4:3
17852.text: Whoever remains in Zion and is left over in Jerusalem will be called holy, all of those in Jerusalem written down for life.

17853.label: Isaiah 4:4
17853.text: When Jehovah washes away the filth of the daughters of Zion and rinses away the bloodshed of Jerusalem from her midst by the spirit of judgment and by a spirit of burning,

17854.label: Isaiah 4:5
17854.text: Jehovah will also create over the whole site of Mount Zion and over the place of her conventions a cloud and smoke by day and a bright flaming fire by night; for over all the glory there will be a shelter.

17855.label: Isaiah 4:6
17855.text: And there will be a booth for shade by day from the heat, and for refuge and protection from storms and the rain.

17856.label: Isaiah 5:1
17856.text: Let me sing, please, to my belovedA song about my loved one and his vineyard. My beloved had a vineyard on a fruitful hillside.

17857.label: Isaiah 5:2
17857.text: He dug it up and rid it of stones. He planted it with a choice red vine,Built a tower in the middle of it,And hewed out a winepress in it. Then he kept hoping for it to produce grapes,But it produced only wild grapes.

17858.label: Isaiah 5:3
17858.text: “And now, you inhabitants of Jerusalem and men of Judah,Please judge between me and my vineyard.

17859.label: Isaiah 5:4
17859.text: What more could I have done for my vineyardThat I have not already done? Why, when I hoped for grapes,Did it produce only wild grapes?

17860.label: Isaiah 5:5
17860.text: Now, please, let me tell youWhat I will do to my vineyard: I will remove its hedge,And it will be burned down. I will break down its stone wall,And it will be trampled on.

17861.label: Isaiah 5:6
17861.text: I will make it a wasteland; It will not be pruned or hoed. It will be overgrown with thornbushes and weeds, And I will command the clouds not to send any rain on it.

17862.label: Isaiah 5:7
17862.text: For the vineyard of Jehovah of armies is the house of Israel; The men of Judah are the plantation he was fond of. He kept hoping for justice, But look! there was injustice;For righteousness,But look! a cry of distress.”

17863.label: Isaiah 5:8
17863.text: Woe to those who join one house to another house And who annex one field to another field Until there is no more roomAnd you live by yourselves on the land!

17864.label: Isaiah 5:9
17864.text: Jehovah of armies has sworn in my earsThat many houses, though great and beautiful,Will become an object of horror,Without an inhabitant.

17865.label: Isaiah 5:10
17865.text: For ten acres of vineyard will produce but one bath measure, And a hoʹmer measure of seed will produce only an eʹphah.

17866.label: Isaiah 5:11
17866.text: Woe to those who get up early in the morning to drink alcohol, Who linger late into the evening darkness until wine inflames them!

17867.label: Isaiah 5:12
17867.text: They have harp and stringed instrument,Tambourine, flute, and wine at their feasts;But they do not consider the activity of Jehovah,And they do not see the work of his hands.

17868.label: Isaiah 5:13
17868.text: So my people will go into exileFor lack of knowledge; Their glorious men will go hungry, And all their people will be parched with thirst.

17869.label: Isaiah 5:14
17869.text: So the Grave has enlarged itself And has opened its mouth wide without limit; And her splendor, her noisy multitudes, and her revelersWill certainly go down into it.

17870.label: Isaiah 5:15
17870.text: And man will bow down,Man will be brought low,And the eyes of the haughty will be brought low.

17871.label: Isaiah 5:16
17871.text: Jehovah of armies will be exalted by his judgment; The true God, the Holy One, will sanctify himself through righteousness.

17872.label: Isaiah 5:17
17872.text: And the lambs will graze as in their pasture;Foreign residents will feed on the desolate places of well-fed animals.

17873.label: Isaiah 5:18
17873.text: Woe to those who drag along their guilt with ropes of deceptionAnd their sin with wagon cords;

17874.label: Isaiah 5:19
17874.text: Those who say: “Let Him speed up his work;Let it come quickly that we may see it. Let the purpose of the Holy One of Israel take placeThat we may know it!”

17875.label: Isaiah 5:20
17875.text: Woe to those who say that good is bad and bad is good, Those who substitute darkness for light and light for darkness,Those who put bitter for sweet and sweet for bitter!

17876.label: Isaiah 5:21
17876.text: Woe to those wise in their own eyesAnd discreet in their own sight!

17877.label: Isaiah 5:22
17877.text: Woe to those who are mighty in drinking wineAnd to the men who are masters at mixing alcoholic drinks,

17878.label: Isaiah 5:23
17878.text: Those who acquit the wicked for a bribe And who deny justice to the righteous!

17879.label: Isaiah 5:24
17879.text: Therefore, just as the tongue of fire consumes the stubbleAnd dry grass shrivels in the flames,Their very roots will rot,And their blossoms will scatter like powder,Because they rejected the law of Jehovah of armiesAnd disrespected the word of the Holy One of Israel.

17880.label: Isaiah 5:25
17880.text: That is why the anger of Jehovah burns against his people,And he will stretch out his hand against them and strike them. The mountains will quake,And their corpses will be like refuse in the streets. In view of all this, his anger has not turned back,But his hand is still stretched out to strike.

17881.label: Isaiah 5:26
17881.text: He has raised up a signal to a distant nation; He has whistled for them to come from the ends of the earth; And look! they are coming very swiftly.

17882.label: Isaiah 5:27
17882.text: None among them are tired or stumbling. No one is drowsy or sleeps. The belt around their waist is not loosened,Nor are their sandal laces broken.

17883.label: Isaiah 5:28
17883.text: All their arrows are sharp,And all their bows are bent. The hooves of their horses are like flint,And their wheels like a storm wind.

17884.label: Isaiah 5:29
17884.text: Their roaring is like that of a lion;They roar like young lions. They will growl and seize the preyAnd carry it off with no one to rescue it.

17885.label: Isaiah 5:30
17885.text: In that day they will growl over itLike the growling of the sea. Anyone who gazes at the land will see distressing darkness;Even the light has grown dark because of the clouds.

17886.label: Isaiah 6:1
17886.text: In the year that King Uz·ziʹah died, I saw Jehovah sitting on a lofty and elevated throne, and the skirts of his robe filled the temple.

17887.label: Isaiah 6:2
17887.text: Seraphs were standing above him; each had six wings. Each covered his face with two and covered his feet with two, and each of them would fly about with two.

17888.label: Isaiah 6:3
17888.text: And one called to the other: “Holy, holy, holy is Jehovah of armies. The whole earth is filled with his glory.”

17889.label: Isaiah 6:4
17889.text: And the pivots of the thresholds quivered at the sound of the shouting, and the house was filled with smoke.

17890.label: Isaiah 6:5
17890.text: Then I said: “Woe to me! I am as good as dead, For I am a man of unclean lips,And I live among a people of unclean lips; For my eyes have seen the King, Jehovah of armies himself!”

17891.label: Isaiah 6:6
17891.text: At that, one of the seraphs flew to me, and in his hand was a glowing coal that he had taken with tongs from the altar.

17892.label: Isaiah 6:7
17892.text: He touched my mouth and said: “Look! This has touched your lips. Your guilt is removed,And your sin is atoned for.”

17893.label: Isaiah 6:8
17893.text: Then I heard the voice of Jehovah saying: “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” And I said: “Here I am! Send me!”

17894.label: Isaiah 6:9
17894.text: And he replied, “Go, and say to this people: ‘You will hear again and again,But you will not understand;You will see again and again,But you will not get any knowledge.’

17895.label: Isaiah 6:10
17895.text: Make the heart of this people unreceptive, Make their ears unresponsive, And paste their eyes together,So that they may not see with their eyesAnd hear with their ears,So that their heart may not understandAnd they may not turn back and be healed.”

17896.label: Isaiah 6:11
17896.text: At this I said: “How long, O Jehovah?” Then he said: “Until the cities crash in ruins without an inhabitantAnd the houses are without peopleAnd the land is ruined and desolate;

17897.label: Isaiah 6:12
17897.text: Until Jehovah removes men far away And the deserted condition of the land becomes very extensive.

17898.label: Isaiah 6:13
17898.text: “But there will still be a tenth in it, and it will again be burned, like a big tree and like an oak, which after they are cut down leave a stump; a holy seed will be its stump.”

17899.label: Isaiah 7:1
17899.text: Now in the days of Aʹhaz son of Joʹtham son of Uz·ziʹah, the king of Judah, King Reʹzin of Syria and Peʹkah son of Rem·a·liʹah, the king of Israel, came up to wage war against Jerusalem, but he could not capture it.

17900.label: Isaiah 7:2
17900.text: A report was made to the house of David: “Syria has joined forces with Eʹphra·im.” And the heart of Aʹhaz and the heart of his people began to tremble, like the trees of the forest shaking in the wind.

17901.label: Isaiah 7:3
17901.text: Jehovah then said to Isaiah: “Go out, please, to meet Aʹhaz, you and your son Sheʹar-jaʹshub, at the end of the conduit of the upper pool by the highway of the laundryman’s field.

17902.label: Isaiah 7:4
17902.text: You must say to him, ‘Take care to stay calm. Do not be afraid, and do not lose heart because of these two stumps of smoldering logs, because of the hot anger of Reʹzin and Syria and the son of Rem·a·liʹah.

17903.label: Isaiah 7:5
17903.text: For Syria with Eʹphra·im and the son of Rem·a·liʹah have plotted harm against you, saying:

17904.label: Isaiah 7:6
17904.text: “Let us go up against Judah and tear it apart and conquer it for ourselves, and let us appoint the son of Tabʹe·el as its king.”

17905.label: Isaiah 7:7
17905.text: “‘This is what the Sovereign Lord Jehovah says: “It will not succeed,Nor will it take place.

17906.label: Isaiah 7:8
17906.text: For the head of Syria is Damascus,And the head of Damascus is Reʹzin. Within just 65 yearsEʹphra·im will be completely shattered and cease to be a people.

17907.label: Isaiah 7:9
17907.text: The head of Eʹphra·im is Sa·marʹi·a, And the head of Sa·marʹi·a is the son of Rem·a·liʹah. Unless you have firm faith,You will not be firmly established.”’”

17909.label: Isaiah 7:11
17909.text: “Ask for a sign from Jehovah your God; it may be as deep as the Grave or as high as the sky.”

17910.label: Isaiah 7:12
17910.text: But Aʹhaz said: “I will not ask, nor will I put Jehovah to the test.”

17911.label: Isaiah 7:13
17911.text: Isaiah then said: “Listen, please, O house of David. Is it not enough that you try the patience of men? Must you also try the patience of God?

17912.label: Isaiah 7:14
17912.text: Therefore, Jehovah himself will give you a sign: Look! The young woman will become pregnant and will give birth to a son, and she will name him Im·manʹu·el.

17913.label: Isaiah 7:15
17913.text: He will eat butter and honey by the time that he knows how to reject the bad and choose the good.

17914.label: Isaiah 7:16
17914.text: For before the boy knows how to reject the bad and choose the good, the land of the two kings whom you dread will be completely abandoned.

17915.label: Isaiah 7:17
17915.text: Jehovah will bring against you and against your people and against the house of your father a time such as has not come since the day Eʹphra·im broke away from Judah, for He will bring the king of As·syrʹi·a.

17916.label: Isaiah 7:18
17916.text: “In that day Jehovah will whistle for the flies from the distant streams of the Nile of Egypt and for the bees in the land of As·syrʹi·a,

17917.label: Isaiah 7:19
17917.text: and they will all come and settle down on the steep valleys, on the rocky clefts, on all the thornbushes, and on all the watering places.

17918.label: Isaiah 7:20
17918.text: “In that day by means of a hired razor from the region of the River, by means of the king of As·syrʹi·a, Jehovah will shave the head and the hair of the legs, and it will sweep away the beard as well.

17919.label: Isaiah 7:21
17919.text: “In that day a man will keep alive a young cow of the herd and two sheep.

17920.label: Isaiah 7:22
17920.text: And because of the abundance of milk, he will eat butter, for everyone remaining in the land will eat butter and honey.

17921.label: Isaiah 7:23
17921.text: “In that day wherever there used to be 1,000 vines worth 1,000 pieces of silver, there will be only thornbushes and weeds.

17922.label: Isaiah 7:24
17922.text: Men will go there with bow and arrow, because all the land will become thornbushes and weeds.

17923.label: Isaiah 7:25
17923.text: And all the mountains that used to be cleared with a hoe, you will not go near for fear of thornbushes and weeds; they will become a grazing place for bulls and a trampling ground of sheep.”

17924.label: Isaiah 8:1
17924.text: Jehovah said to me: “Take a large tablet and write on it with an ordinary stylus, ‘Maʹher-shalʹal-hash-baz.’

17925.label: Isaiah 8:2
17925.text: And let me have it confirmed in writing by faithful witnesses, U·riʹah the priest and Zech·a·riʹah the son of Je·ber·e·chiʹah.”

17926.label: Isaiah 8:3
17926.text: Then I had relations with the prophetess, and she became pregnant and in time gave birth to a son. Jehovah then said to me: “Name him Maʹher-shalʹal-hash-baz,

17927.label: Isaiah 8:4
17927.text: for before the boy knows how to call out, ‘My father!’ and ‘My mother!’ the resources of Damascus and the spoil of Sa·marʹi·a will be carried away before the king of As·syrʹi·a.”

17929.label: Isaiah 8:6
17929.text: “Because this people has rejected the gently flowing waters of the Shi·loʹah And they rejoice over Reʹzin and the son of Rem·a·liʹah,

17930.label: Isaiah 8:7
17930.text: Therefore look! Jehovah will bring against themThe mighty and vast waters of the River, The king of As·syrʹi·a and all his glory. He will come up over all his streambedsAnd overflow all his banks

17931.label: Isaiah 8:8
17931.text: And sweep through Judah. He will flood and pass through, reaching to the neck; His outspread wings will fill the breadth of your land,O Im·manʹu·el!”

17932.label: Isaiah 8:9
17932.text: Cause harm, you peoples, but you will be shattered to pieces. Listen, all you from distant parts of the earth! Prepare for battle, but you will be shattered to pieces! Prepare for battle, but you will be shattered to pieces!

17933.label: Isaiah 8:10
17933.text: Devise a plan, but it will be thwarted! Say what you like, but it will not succeed,For God is with us!

17934.label: Isaiah 8:11
17934.text: With his strong hand on me, this is what Jehovah said to me to warn me away from following the course of this people:

17935.label: Isaiah 8:12
17935.text: “You should not call a conspiracy what this people calls a conspiracy! Do not fear what they fear;Do not tremble at it.

17936.label: Isaiah 8:13
17936.text: Jehovah of armies—he is the One you should regard as holy, He is the One you should fear,And he is the One who should cause you to tremble.”

17937.label: Isaiah 8:14
17937.text: He will become as a sanctuary,But as a stone to strike againstAnd as a rock to stumble over To both houses of Israel,As a trap and a snareTo the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

17938.label: Isaiah 8:15
17938.text: Many of them will stumble and fall and be broken;They will be ensnared and caught.

17939.label: Isaiah 8:16
17939.text: Wrap up the written confirmation; Seal up the law among my disciples!

17940.label: Isaiah 8:17
17940.text: I will keep in expectation of Jehovah, who is hiding his face from the house of Jacob, and I will hope in him.

17941.label: Isaiah 8:18
17941.text: Look! I and the children whom Jehovah has given me are as signs and as miracles in Israel from Jehovah of armies, who resides on Mount Zion.

17942.label: Isaiah 8:19
17942.text: And if they say to you: “Inquire of the spirit mediums or of the fortune-tellers who chirp and mutter,” is it not of their God that a people should inquire? Should they inquire of the dead in behalf of the living?

17943.label: Isaiah 8:20
17943.text: Instead, they should inquire of the law and of the written confirmation! When they do not speak according to this word, they have no light.

17944.label: Isaiah 8:21
17944.text: And each one will pass through the land afflicted and hungry; and because he is hungry and indignant, he will curse his king and his God as he looks upward.

17945.label: Isaiah 8:22
17945.text: Then he will look to the earth and see only distress and darkness, obscurity and hard times, gloom and no brightness.

17946.label: Isaiah 9:1
17946.text: However, the gloom will not be as when the land had distress, as in former times when the land of Zebʹu·lun and the land of Naphʹta·li were treated with contempt. But at a later time He will cause it to be honored—the way by the sea, in the region of the Jordan, Galʹi·lee of the nations.

17947.label: Isaiah 9:2
17947.text: The people who were walking in the darknessHave seen a great light. As for those dwelling in the land of deep shadow,Light has shone on them.

17948.label: Isaiah 9:3
17948.text: You have made the nation populous;You have made its rejoicing great. They rejoice before youAs people rejoice in the harvesttime,As those who joyfully divide up the spoil.

17949.label: Isaiah 9:4
17949.text: For you have shattered to pieces the yoke of their load,The rod on their shoulders, the staff of the taskmaster,As in the day of Midʹi·an.

17950.label: Isaiah 9:5
17950.text: Every boot that shakes the earth as it marchesAnd every garment soaked in bloodWill become fuel for the fire.

17951.label: Isaiah 9:6
17951.text: For a child has been born to us, A son has been given to us;And the rulership will rest on his shoulder. His name will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Eternal Father, Prince of Peace.

17952.label: Isaiah 9:7
17952.text: To the increase of his rulership And to peace, there will be no end, On the throne of David and on his kingdomIn order to establish it firmly and to sustain itThrough justice and righteousness, From now on and forever. The zeal of Jehovah of armies will do this.

17953.label: Isaiah 9:8
17953.text: Jehovah sent a word against Jacob,And it has come against Israel.

17954.label: Isaiah 9:9
17954.text: And all the people will know it—Eʹphra·im and the inhabitants of Sa·marʹi·a—Who say in their haughtiness and in their insolence of heart:

17955.label: Isaiah 9:10
17955.text: “Bricks have fallen,But we will build with hewn stone. Sycamore trees have been cut down,But we will replace them with cedars.”

17956.label: Isaiah 9:11
17956.text: Jehovah will raise up Reʹzin’s adversaries against himAnd will stir his enemies to action,

17957.label: Isaiah 9:12
17957.text: Syria from the east and the Phi·lisʹtines from the west, They will devour Israel with open mouths. In view of all this, his anger has not turned back,But his hand is still stretched out to strike.

17958.label: Isaiah 9:13
17958.text: For the people have not returned to the One who strikes them;They have not sought Jehovah of armies.

17959.label: Isaiah 9:14
17959.text: Jehovah will cut off from IsraelHead and tail, shoot and rush, in one day.

17960.label: Isaiah 9:15
17960.text: The elder and highly respected one is the head,And the prophet giving false instruction is the tail.

17961.label: Isaiah 9:16
17961.text: Those leading this people are causing them to wander,And those who are being led are confused.

17962.label: Isaiah 9:17
17962.text: That is why Jehovah will not rejoice over their young men,And he will have no mercy on their fatherless children and their widowsBecause all of them are apostates and evildoers And every mouth is speaking senselessness. In view of all this, his anger has not turned back,But his hand is still stretched out to strike.

17963.label: Isaiah 9:18
17963.text: For wickedness burns like a fire,Consuming thornbushes and weeds. It will set fire to the thickets of the forest,And they will go up in clouds of smoke.

17964.label: Isaiah 9:19
17964.text: In the fury of Jehovah of armiesThe land has been set on fire,And the people will become fuel for the fire. No one will spare even his brother.

17965.label: Isaiah 9:20
17965.text: One will cut down on the rightBut still be hungry;And one will eat on the leftBut will not be satisfied. Each will devour the flesh of his own arm,

17966.label: Isaiah 9:21
17966.text: Ma·nasʹseh will devour Eʹphra·im,And Eʹphra·im Ma·nasʹseh. Together they will be against Judah. In view of all this, his anger has not turned back,But his hand is still stretched out to strike.

17967.label: Isaiah 10:1
17967.text: Woe to those who enact harmful regulations, Who constantly draft oppressive decrees,

17968.label: Isaiah 10:2
17968.text: To deny the legal claim of the poor,To deprive the lowly among my people of justice, Making widows their spoilAnd fatherless children their plunder!

17969.label: Isaiah 10:3
17969.text: What will you do on the day of reckoning, When destruction comes from afar? To whom will you flee for assistance, And where will you leave your wealth?

17970.label: Isaiah 10:4
17970.text: Nothing remains except to crouch among the prisonersOr to fall among the slain. In view of all this, his anger has not turned back,But his hand is still stretched out to strike.

17971.label: Isaiah 10:5
17971.text: “Aha! the As·syrʹi·an, The rod to express my anger And the staff in their hand for my denunciation!

17972.label: Isaiah 10:6
17972.text: I will send him against an apostate nation, Against the people who infuriated me;I will command him to take much spoil and much plunderAnd to trample them like mud in the streets.

17973.label: Isaiah 10:7
17973.text: But he will not be inclined this wayAnd his heart will not scheme this way;For it is in his heart to annihilate,To cut off many nations, not a few.

17974.label: Isaiah 10:8
17974.text: For he says,‘Are not my princes all kings?

17975.label: Isaiah 10:9
17975.text: Is not Calʹno just like Carʹche·mish? Is not Haʹmath like Arʹpad? Is not Sa·marʹi·a like Damascus?

17976.label: Isaiah 10:10
17976.text: My hand has seized the kingdoms of the worthless gods,Whose graven images were more than those of Jerusalem and Sa·marʹi·a!

17977.label: Isaiah 10:11
17977.text: Will I not also do to Jerusalem and her idolsJust as I have done to Sa·marʹi·a and to her worthless gods?’

17978.label: Isaiah 10:12
17978.text: “When Jehovah finishes all his work on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, He will punish the king of As·syrʹi·a for his insolent heart and his proud, arrogant gaze.

17979.label: Isaiah 10:13
17979.text: For he says,‘I will do this by the strength of my handAnd with my wisdom, for I am wise. I will remove the boundaries of peoples And pillage their treasures, And I will subdue the inhabitants like a mighty one.

17980.label: Isaiah 10:14
17980.text: Like a man reaching into a nest,My hand will seize the resources of the peoples;And like one gathering abandoned eggs,I will gather the whole earth! No one will flutter his wings or open his mouth or chirp.’”

17981.label: Isaiah 10:15
17981.text: Will the ax exalt itself over the one who chops with it? Will the saw exalt itself over the one who saws with it? Could a staff wave the one who lifts it? Or could a rod lift up the one who is not made of wood?

17982.label: Isaiah 10:16
17982.text: Therefore the true Lord, Jehovah of armies,Will inflict emaciation on his fat ones, And beneath his glory he will kindle a blazing fire.

17983.label: Isaiah 10:17
17983.text: Israel’s Light will become a fire, And his Holy One a flame;It will blaze up and consume his weeds and his thornbushes in one day.

17984.label: Isaiah 10:18
17984.text: He will utterly do away with the glory of his forest and his orchard;It will be as when a sick man wastes away.

17985.label: Isaiah 10:19
17985.text: The rest of the trees of his forestWill be so few that a boy could list them.

17986.label: Isaiah 10:20
17986.text: In that day those remaining of IsraelAnd the survivors of the house of JacobWill no longer support themselves on the one who struck them; But they will support themselves on Jehovah,The Holy One of Israel, with faithfulness.

17987.label: Isaiah 10:21
17987.text: Only a remnant will return,The remnant of Jacob, to the Mighty God.

17988.label: Isaiah 10:22
17988.text: For though your people, O Israel,Are as the grains of sand of the sea,Only a remnant of them will return. An extermination has been decided on, And justice will engulf them.

17989.label: Isaiah 10:23
17989.text: Yes, the extermination decided on by the Sovereign Lord, Jehovah of armies,Will be carried out in the entire land.

17990.label: Isaiah 10:24
17990.text: Therefore this is what the Sovereign Lord, Jehovah of armies, says: “Do not be afraid, my people who are dwelling in Zion, because of the As·syrʹi·an, who used to strike you with the rod and to lift up his staff against you as Egypt did.

17991.label: Isaiah 10:25
17991.text: For in a very little while the denunciation will come to an end; my anger will be directed to their destruction.

17992.label: Isaiah 10:26
17992.text: Jehovah of armies will brandish a whip against him, as when he defeated Midʹi·an by the rock Oʹreb. And his staff will be over the sea, and he will raise it as he did with Egypt.

17993.label: Isaiah 10:27
17993.text: In that day his load will depart from on your shoulder, And his yoke from on your neck, And the yoke will be broken because of the oil.”

17994.label: Isaiah 10:28
17994.text: He has come to Aiʹath; He has passed through Migʹron;At Michʹmash he deposits his baggage.

17995.label: Isaiah 10:29
17995.text: They have passed over the ford;They spend the night at Geʹba; Raʹmah trembles, Gibʹe·ah of Saul has fled.

17996.label: Isaiah 10:30
17996.text: Cry out and scream, O daughter of Galʹlim! Pay attention, O Laʹi·shah! O poor Anʹa·thoth!

17997.label: Isaiah 10:31
17997.text: Mad·meʹnah has run away. The inhabitants of Geʹbim have sought shelter.

17998.label: Isaiah 10:32
17998.text: This very day he will halt in Nob. He shakes his fist at the mountain of the daughter of Zion,The hill of Jerusalem.

17999.label: Isaiah 10:33
17999.text: Look! The true Lord, Jehovah of armies,Is chopping off branches with a terrible crash; The tallest trees are being cut down,And the lofty are brought low.

18000.label: Isaiah 10:34
18000.text: He strikes down the thickets of the forest with an iron tool, And Lebʹa·non will fall by a mighty one.

18001.label: Isaiah 11:1
18001.text: A twig will grow out of the stump of Jesʹse, And a sprout from his roots will bear fruit.

18002.label: Isaiah 11:2
18002.text: And the spirit of Jehovah will settle upon him, The spirit of wisdom and of understanding,The spirit of counsel and of mightiness, The spirit of knowledge and of the fear of Jehovah.

18003.label: Isaiah 11:3
18003.text: And he will find delight in the fear of Jehovah. He will not judge by what appears to his eyes,Nor reprove simply according to what his ears hear.

18004.label: Isaiah 11:4
18004.text: He will judge the lowly with fairness, And with uprightness he will give reproof in behalf of the meek ones of the earth. He will strike the earth with the rod of his mouth And put the wicked to death with the breath of his lips.

18005.label: Isaiah 11:5
18005.text: Righteousness will be the belt around his waist,And faithfulness the belt of his hips.

18006.label: Isaiah 11:6
18006.text: The wolf will reside for a while with the lamb, And with the young goat the leopard will lie down,And the calf and the lion and the fattened animal will all be together; And a little boy will lead them.

18007.label: Isaiah 11:7
18007.text: The cow and the bear will feed together,And their young will lie down together. The lion will eat straw like the bull.

18008.label: Isaiah 11:8
18008.text: The nursing child will play over the lair of a cobra,And a weaned child will put his hand over the den of a poisonous snake.

18009.label: Isaiah 11:9
18009.text: They will not cause any harm Or any ruin in all my holy mountain, Because the earth will certainly be filled with the knowledge of JehovahAs the waters cover the sea.

18010.label: Isaiah 11:10
18010.text: In that day the root of Jesʹse will stand up as a signal for the peoples. To him the nations will turn for guidance, And his resting-place will become glorious.

18011.label: Isaiah 11:11
18011.text: In that day Jehovah will again offer his hand, a second time, to reclaim the remnant of his people who are left from As·syrʹi·a, from Egypt, from Pathʹros, from Cush, from Eʹlam, from Shiʹnar, from Haʹmath, and from the islands of the sea.

18012.label: Isaiah 11:12
18012.text: He will raise up a signal for the nations and gather the dispersed ones of Israel, and he will gather together the scattered ones of Judah from the four corners of the earth.

18013.label: Isaiah 11:13
18013.text: The jealousy of Eʹphra·im will be gone, And those who show hostility to Judah will be done away with. Eʹphra·im will not be jealous of Judah,Nor will Judah show hostility toward Eʹphra·im.

18014.label: Isaiah 11:14
18014.text: And they will swoop down on the slopes of the Phi·lisʹtines to the west;Together they will plunder the people of the East. They will thrust out their hand against Eʹdom and Moʹab, And the Amʹmon·ites will become their subjects.

18015.label: Isaiah 11:15
18015.text: Jehovah will divide the gulf of the Egyptian sea And wave his hand over the River. With his scorching breath he will strike it in its seven torrents,And he will cause people to walk across in their sandals.

18016.label: Isaiah 11:16
18016.text: And there will be a highway out of As·syrʹi·a for the remnant of his people who are left, As there was for Israel in the day he came out of the land of Egypt.

18017.label: Isaiah 12:1
18017.text: In that day you will certainly say: “I thank you, O Jehovah,For although you were angry with me,Your anger gradually subsided, and you comforted me.

18018.label: Isaiah 12:2
18018.text: Look! God is my salvation. I will trust and feel no dread; For Jah Jehovah is my strength and my might,And he has become my salvation.”

18019.label: Isaiah 12:3
18019.text: With rejoicing you will draw waterFrom the springs of salvation.

18020.label: Isaiah 12:4
18020.text: And in that day you will say: “Give thanks to Jehovah, call on his name,Make his deeds known among the peoples! Declare that his name is exalted.

18021.label: Isaiah 12:5
18021.text: Sing praises to Jehovah, for he has done magnificent things. Let this be made known in all the earth.

18022.label: Isaiah 12:6
18022.text: Cry out and shout for joy, you inhabitant of Zion,For great in your midst is the Holy One of Israel.”

18023.label: Isaiah 13:1
18023.text: A pronouncement against Babylon that Isaiah the son of Aʹmoz saw in vision:

18024.label: Isaiah 13:2
18024.text: “Raise up a signal on a mountain of bare rocks. Call out to them, wave your hand,So that they may come into the entrances of the nobles.

18025.label: Isaiah 13:3
18025.text: I have issued the command to those whom I have appointed. I have summoned my warriors to express my anger,My proudly exultant ones.

18026.label: Isaiah 13:4
18026.text: Listen! A crowd in the mountains;It sounds like a numerous people! Listen! The uproar of kingdoms,Of nations gathered together! Jehovah of armies is mustering the army for war.

18027.label: Isaiah 13:5
18027.text: They are coming from a distant land, From the extremity of the heavens,Jehovah and the weapons of his wrath,To bring ruin to all the earth.

18028.label: Isaiah 13:6
18028.text: Wail, for the day of Jehovah is near! It will come as a destruction from the Almighty.

18029.label: Isaiah 13:7
18029.text: That is why all hands will go limp,And every man’s heart will melt with fear.

18030.label: Isaiah 13:8
18030.text: The people are panic-stricken. They are seized with convulsions and pain,Like a woman in labor. They look at one another in horror,With faces inflamed by anguish.

18031.label: Isaiah 13:9
18031.text: Look! The day of Jehovah is coming,Cruel both with fury and with burning anger,To make the land an object of horror, And to annihilate the land’s sinners from it.

18032.label: Isaiah 13:10
18032.text: For the stars of the heavens and their constellations Will not give off their light;The sun will be dark when it rises,And the moon will not shed its light.

18033.label: Isaiah 13:11
18033.text: I will call the inhabited earth to account for its badness, And the wicked for their error. I will put an end to the pride of the presumptuous,And I will humble the haughtiness of tyrants.

18034.label: Isaiah 13:12
18034.text: I will make mortal man scarcer than refined gold, And humans scarcer than the gold of Oʹphir.

18035.label: Isaiah 13:13
18035.text: That is why I will make the heavens tremble,And the earth will be shaken out of its place At the fury of Jehovah of armies in the day of his burning anger.

18036.label: Isaiah 13:14
18036.text: Like a hunted gazelle and like a flock with no one to gather them,Each will return to his own people;Each will flee to his own land.

18037.label: Isaiah 13:15
18037.text: Whoever is found will be pierced through,And whoever is caught will fall by the sword.

18038.label: Isaiah 13:16
18038.text: Their children will be dashed to pieces before their eyes, Their houses will be looted,And their wives will be raped.

18039.label: Isaiah 13:17
18039.text: Here I am raising up against them the Medes, Who regard silver as nothingAnd who take no delight in gold.

18040.label: Isaiah 13:18
18040.text: Their bows will shatter young men; They will show no pity on the fruit of the wombNor mercy to children.

18041.label: Isaiah 13:19
18041.text: And Babylon, the most glorious of kingdoms, The beauty and the pride of the Chal·deʹans, Will be like Sodʹom and Go·morʹrah when God overthrew them.

18042.label: Isaiah 13:20
18042.text: She will never be inhabited,Nor will she be a place to reside in throughout all generations. No Arab will pitch his tent there,And no shepherds will rest their flocks there.

18043.label: Isaiah 13:21
18043.text: The desert creatures will lie down there;Their houses will be filled with eagle owls. The ostriches will reside there, And wild goats will skip about there.

18044.label: Isaiah 13:22
18044.text: Howling creatures will cry out in her towers,And jackals in her luxurious palaces. Her time is near, and her days will not be prolonged.”

18045.label: Isaiah 14:1
18045.text: For Jehovah will show mercy to Jacob, and he will again choose Israel. He will settle them in their land, and the foreign residents will join them and attach themselves to the house of Jacob.

18046.label: Isaiah 14:2
18046.text: And peoples will take them and bring them to their own place, and the house of Israel will possess them as male and female servants in Jehovah’s land; and they will be the captors of those who held them captive, and they will have in subjection those who were forcing them to work.

18047.label: Isaiah 14:3
18047.text: In the day when Jehovah gives you rest from your pain and from your turmoil and from the hard slavery imposed on you,

18048.label: Isaiah 14:4
18048.text: you will recite this proverb against the king of Babylon: “How the one forcing others to work has met his end! How the oppression has ended!

18049.label: Isaiah 14:5
18049.text: Jehovah has broken the rod of the wicked,The staff of the rulers,

18050.label: Isaiah 14:6
18050.text: The one furiously striking peoples with unceasing blows, The one angrily subduing nations with relentless persecution.

18051.label: Isaiah 14:7
18051.text: The whole earth now rests, free of disturbance. People cry out for joy.

18052.label: Isaiah 14:8
18052.text: Even the juniper trees rejoice over you,Along with the cedars of Lebʹa·non. They say, ‘Ever since you have fallen,No woodcutter comes up against us.’

18053.label: Isaiah 14:9
18053.text: Even the Grave underneath is stirred upTo meet you when you come. Because of you, it awakens those powerless in death,All the oppressive leaders of the earth. It makes all the kings of the nations rise from their thrones.

18054.label: Isaiah 14:10
18054.text: All of them speak up and say to you,‘Have you also become weak like us? Have you become like us?

18055.label: Isaiah 14:11
18055.text: Down to the Grave your pride has been brought,The sound of your stringed instruments. Maggots are spread beneath you as a bed,And worms are your covering.’

18056.label: Isaiah 14:12
18056.text: How you have fallen from heaven,O shining one, son of the dawn! How you have been cut down to the earth,You who vanquished nations!

18057.label: Isaiah 14:13
18057.text: You said in your heart, ‘I will ascend to the heavens. Above the stars of God I will lift up my throne, And I will sit down on the mountain of meeting,In the remotest parts of the north.

18058.label: Isaiah 14:14
18058.text: I will go up above the tops of the clouds;I will make myself resemble the Most High.’

18059.label: Isaiah 14:15
18059.text: Instead, you will be brought down to the Grave, To the remotest parts of the pit.

18060.label: Isaiah 14:16
18060.text: Those seeing you will stare at you;They will closely examine you, saying,‘Is this the man who was shaking the earth,Who made kingdoms tremble,

18061.label: Isaiah 14:17
18061.text: Who made the inhabited earth like the wildernessAnd overthrew its cities, Who refused to let his prisoners go home?’

18062.label: Isaiah 14:18
18062.text: All other kings of the nations,Yes, all of them, lie down in glory,Each one in his own tomb.

18063.label: Isaiah 14:19
18063.text: But you are discarded without a grave,Like a detested sprout, Clothed with the slain who were stabbed with the sword,Who go down to the stones of a pit,Like a carcass trampled underfoot.

18064.label: Isaiah 14:20
18064.text: You will not join them in a grave,For you destroyed your own land,You killed your own people. The offspring of evildoers will never again be named.

18065.label: Isaiah 14:21
18065.text: Prepare a slaughtering block for his sonsBecause of the guilt of their forefathers,So that they will not rise up and take over the earthAnd fill the land with their cities.”

18066.label: Isaiah 14:22
18066.text: “I will rise up against them,” declares Jehovah of armies. “And I will wipe out from Babylon name and remnant and descendants and posterity,” declares Jehovah.

18067.label: Isaiah 14:23
18067.text: “And I will make her a possession of porcupines and a region of marshes, and I will sweep her with the broom of annihilation,” declares Jehovah of armies.

18068.label: Isaiah 14:24
18068.text: Jehovah of armies has sworn: “Just as I have intended, so it will occur,And just as I have decided, that is what will come true.

18069.label: Isaiah 14:25
18069.text: I will crush the As·syrʹi·an in my land,And I will trample him on my mountains. His yoke will be removed from them,And his load will be removed from their shoulder.”

18070.label: Isaiah 14:26
18070.text: This is what has been decided against all the earth,And this is the hand that is stretched out against all the nations.

18071.label: Isaiah 14:27
18071.text: For Jehovah of armies has decided,And who can thwart it? His hand is stretched out,And who can turn it back?

18072.label: Isaiah 14:28
18072.text: In the year that King Aʹhaz died, this pronouncement was made:

18073.label: Isaiah 14:29
18073.text: “Do not rejoice, Phi·lisʹti·a, any of you,Just because the staff of the one striking you has been broken. For from the root of the serpent will come a poisonous snake, And its offspring will be a flying fiery snake.

18074.label: Isaiah 14:30
18074.text: While the firstborn of the lowly feedAnd the poor lie down in security,I will put your root to death with famine,And what is left of you will be killed.

18075.label: Isaiah 14:31
18075.text: Wail, O gate! Cry out, O city! All of you will lose heart, O Phi·lisʹti·a! For a smoke is coming from the north,And there are no stragglers in his ranks.”

18076.label: Isaiah 14:32
18076.text: How should they answer the messengers of the nation? That Jehovah has laid the foundation of Zion, And that the lowly ones of his people will take refuge in her.

18077.label: Isaiah 15:1
18077.text: A pronouncement against Moʹab: Because it has been devastated in a night,Ar of Moʹab has been silenced. Because it has been devastated in a night,Kir of Moʹab has been silenced.

18078.label: Isaiah 15:2
18078.text: He has gone up to the House and to Diʹbon, To the high places to weep. Moʹab wails over Neʹbo and over Medʹe·ba. Every head is shaved bald, every beard is clipped.

18079.label: Isaiah 15:3
18079.text: In its streets they have put on sackcloth. On their roofs and in their public squares they all wail;They go down weeping.

18080.label: Isaiah 15:4
18080.text: Heshʹbon and E·le·aʹleh cry out;Their voice is heard as far as Jaʹhaz. That is why the armed men of Moʹab keep shouting. He is trembling.

18081.label: Isaiah 15:5
18081.text: My heart cries out over Moʹab. Its fugitives have fled as far as Zoʹar and Egʹlath-she·liʹshi·yah. On the ascent of Luʹhith they weep as they go up;On the way to Hor·o·naʹim they cry out over the catastrophe.

18082.label: Isaiah 15:6
18082.text: For the waters of Nimʹrim are desolate;The green grass has dried up,The grass is gone and nothing green is left.

18083.label: Isaiah 15:7
18083.text: That is why they are carrying away what is left of their stores and their riches;They are crossing the valley of poplars.

18084.label: Isaiah 15:8
18084.text: For the outcry echoes throughout the territory of Moʹab. The wailing reaches to Eg·laʹim;The wailing reaches to Beʹer-eʹlim.

18085.label: Isaiah 15:9
18085.text: For the waters of Diʹmon are full of blood,And I have more in store for Diʹmon: A lion for those of Moʹab who escapeAnd for those remaining in the land.

18086.label: Isaiah 16:1
18086.text: Send a ram to the ruler of the land,From Seʹla through the wildernessTo the mountain of the daughter of Zion.

18087.label: Isaiah 16:2
18087.text: Like a bird chased away from its nest, So the daughters of Moʹab will be at the fords of Arʹnon.

18088.label: Isaiah 16:3
18088.text: “Offer counsel, carry out the decision. Make your shadow at high noon like the night. Conceal the dispersed and do not betray those fleeing.

18089.label: Isaiah 16:4
18089.text: May my dispersed ones reside in you, O Moʹab. Become a place of concealment to them because of the destroyer. The oppressor will reach his end,The destruction will come to an end,And those trampling others down will perish from the earth.

18090.label: Isaiah 16:5
18090.text: Then a throne will be firmly established in loyal love. The one who sits on it in the tent of David will be faithful; He will judge fairly and will swiftly execute righteousness.”

18091.label: Isaiah 16:6
18091.text: We have heard about the pride of Moʹab—he is very proud —His haughtiness and his pride and his fury; But his empty talk will come to nothing.

18092.label: Isaiah 16:7
18092.text: So Moʹab will wail for Moʹab;They will all wail. Those who are stricken will moan for the raisin cakes of Kir-harʹe·seth.

18093.label: Isaiah 16:8
18093.text: For the terraces of Heshʹbon have withered,The vine of Sibʹmah, The rulers of the nations have trampled its bright-red branches; They had reached as far as Jaʹzer; They had extended into the wilderness. Its shoots had spread out and gone as far as the sea.

18094.label: Isaiah 16:9
18094.text: That is why I will weep over the vine of Sibʹmah as I weep for Jaʹzer. With my tears I will drench you, O Heshʹbon and E·le·aʹleh, Because the shouting over your summer fruit and your harvest has ended.

18095.label: Isaiah 16:10
18095.text: Rejoicing and joyfulness have been taken away from the orchard,And there are no songs of joy or shouting in the vineyards. The treader no longer treads out wine in the presses,For I have caused the shouting to cease.

18096.label: Isaiah 16:11
18096.text: That is why deep within me I am boisterous over Moʹab, Like the strumming of a harp,And my innermost being over Kir-harʹe·seth.

18097.label: Isaiah 16:12
18097.text: Even when Moʹab wears himself out on the high place and goes to pray in his sanctuary, he will accomplish nothing.

18098.label: Isaiah 16:13
18098.text: This is the word that Jehovah previously spoke concerning Moʹab.

18099.label: Isaiah 16:14
18099.text: And now Jehovah says: “Within three years, like the years of a hired worker, the glory of Moʹab will be disgraced with much tumult of every sort, and those who remain will be very few and insignificant.”

18100.label: Isaiah 17:1
18100.text: A pronouncement against Damascus: “Look! Damascus will cease to be a city,And it will become a heap of ruins.

18101.label: Isaiah 17:2
18101.text: The cities of A·roʹer will be abandoned;They will become places for flocks to lie downWith no one to make them afraid.

18102.label: Isaiah 17:3
18102.text: Fortified cities will disappear from Eʹphra·im, And the kingdom from Damascus; And those remaining of SyriaWill be like the glory of the Israelites,” declares Jehovah of armies.

18103.label: Isaiah 17:4
18103.text: “In that day the glory of Jacob will diminish,And his healthy body will grow thin.

18104.label: Isaiah 17:5
18104.text: It will be as when the harvester is gathering the standing grainAnd his arm harvests the ears of grain,Like when one gleans grain in the Valley of Rephʹa·im.

18105.label: Isaiah 17:6
18105.text: Only gleanings will be left,As when an olive tree is beaten: Only two or three ripe olives remain on the highest branch,Only four or five on its fruit-bearing branches,” declares Jehovah the God of Israel.

18106.label: Isaiah 17:7
18106.text: In that day man will look up to his Maker, and his eyes will gaze at the Holy One of Israel.

18107.label: Isaiah 17:8
18107.text: He will not look to the altars, the work of his hands; and he will not gaze at what his fingers have made, either the sacred poles or the incense stands.

18108.label: Isaiah 17:9
18108.text: In that day his fortress cities will become like an abandoned site in the woodland, Like a branch that was abandoned before the Israelites;It will become a wasteland.

18109.label: Isaiah 17:10
18109.text: For you have forgotten the God of your salvation;You have failed to remember the Rock of your fortress. That is why you plant beautiful plantationsAnd set it with the shoot of a stranger.

18110.label: Isaiah 17:11
18110.text: In the day you carefully fence in your plantation,In the morning you make your seed sprout,But the harvest will vanish in the day of disease and incurable pain.

18111.label: Isaiah 17:12
18111.text: Listen! There is a commotion of many peoples,Who are as boisterous as the seas! There is an uproar of nations,Whose sound is like the roar of mighty waters!

18112.label: Isaiah 17:13
18112.text: The nations will make a sound like the roar of many waters. He will rebuke them, and they will flee far away,Chased like the chaff of the mountains before a wind,Like a whirling thistle before a storm wind.

18113.label: Isaiah 17:14
18113.text: In the evening there is terror. Before morning they are no more. This is the share of those pillaging usAnd the lot of those plundering us.

18114.label: Isaiah 18:1
18114.text: Woe to the land of whirring insect wingsIn the region of the rivers of E·thi·oʹpi·a!

18115.label: Isaiah 18:2
18115.text: It sends envoys by sea,Across the waters in papyrus vessels, saying: “Go, you swift messengers,To a tall and smooth-skinned nation, To a people feared everywhere, To a strong, conquering nation, Whose land is washed away by rivers.”

18116.label: Isaiah 18:3
18116.text: All you inhabitants of the land and you residents of the earth,What you see will be like a signal raised on the mountains,And you will hear a sound like the blowing of a horn.

18117.label: Isaiah 18:4
18117.text: For this is what Jehovah said to me: “I will remain undisturbed and look on my established place,Like the shimmering heat along with the sunlight,Like the cloud of dew in the heat of harvest.

18118.label: Isaiah 18:5
18118.text: For before the harvest,When the blossom is finished and the bloom becomes a ripening grape,The shoots will be cut off with pruning shearsAnd the tendrils will be lopped off and removed.

18119.label: Isaiah 18:6
18119.text: They will all be left for the birds of prey of the mountainsAnd for the beasts of the earth. The birds of prey will spend the summer on them,And all the beasts of the earth will spend the harvesttime on them.

18120.label: Isaiah 18:7
18120.text: At that time a gift will be brought to Jehovah of armies,From a tall and smooth-skinned nation, From a people feared everywhere,From a strong, conquering nation, Whose land is washed away by riversTo the place that bears the name of Jehovah of armies, Mount Zion.”

18121.label: Isaiah 19:1
18121.text: A pronouncement against Egypt: Look! Jehovah is riding on a swift cloud and is coming into Egypt. The worthless gods of Egypt will tremble before him, And the heart of Egypt will melt within it.

18122.label: Isaiah 19:2
18122.text: “I will incite Egyptians against Egyptians,And they will fight one another,Each against his brother and his neighbor,City against city, kingdom against kingdom.

18123.label: Isaiah 19:3
18123.text: And the spirit of Egypt will become bewildered within it,And I will confuse its plans. They will resort to the worthless gods,To the charmers and to the spirit mediums and to the fortune-tellers.

18124.label: Isaiah 19:4
18124.text: I will hand Egypt over to a hard master,And a harsh king will rule over them,” declares the true Lord, Jehovah of armies.

18125.label: Isaiah 19:5
18125.text: The water of the sea will be dried up,And the river will become parched and run dry.

18126.label: Isaiah 19:6
18126.text: And the rivers will stink;The Nile canals of Egypt will become low and parched. The reeds and the rushes will decay.

18127.label: Isaiah 19:7
18127.text: The plants along the Nile River, at the mouth of the Nile,And all the land sown with seed along the Nile will dry up. It will be blown away, and it will be no more.

18128.label: Isaiah 19:8
18128.text: And the fishermen will mourn,Those casting fishhooks into the Nile will lament,And those who spread their nets on the water will dwindle.

18129.label: Isaiah 19:9
18129.text: Those who work in combed flax And those making white fabric on the loom will be put to shame.

18130.label: Isaiah 19:10
18130.text: Her weavers will be crushed;All the hired workers will grieve.

18131.label: Isaiah 19:11
18131.text: The princes of Zoʹan are foolish. The wisest advisers of Pharʹaoh give unreasonable advice. How can you say to Pharʹaoh: “I am a descendant of wise ones,A descendant of ancient kings”?

18132.label: Isaiah 19:12
18132.text: Where, then, are your wise men? Let them tell you if they know what Jehovah of armies has decided concerning Egypt.

18133.label: Isaiah 19:13
18133.text: The princes of Zoʹan have acted foolishly;The princes of Noph have been deceived;The chiefs of her tribes have led Egypt astray.

18134.label: Isaiah 19:14
18134.text: Jehovah has poured out on her a spirit of confusion; And they have led Egypt astray in whatever she does,Like a drunk staggering in his vomit.

18135.label: Isaiah 19:15
18135.text: And Egypt will not have any work to do,Whether for the head or the tail, the shoot or the rush.

18136.label: Isaiah 19:16
18136.text: In that day Egypt will become like women, trembling and terrified because of the threatening hand that Jehovah of armies raises against it.

18137.label: Isaiah 19:17
18137.text: And the land of Judah will become a cause for terror to Egypt. They will feel dread at the mention of it because of the decision that Jehovah of armies has made against them.

18138.label: Isaiah 19:18
18138.text: In that day there will be five cities in the land of Egypt speaking the language of Caʹnaan and swearing loyalty to Jehovah of armies. One city will be called The City of Tearing Down.

18139.label: Isaiah 19:19
18139.text: In that day there will be an altar to Jehovah in the middle of the land of Egypt and a pillar to Jehovah at its boundary.

18140.label: Isaiah 19:20
18140.text: It will be for a sign and for a witness to Jehovah of armies in the land of Egypt; for they will cry out to Jehovah because of the oppressors, and he will send them a savior, a grand one, who will save them.

18141.label: Isaiah 19:21
18141.text: And Jehovah will become known to the Egyptians, and the Egyptians will know Jehovah in that day, and they will offer sacrifices and gifts and make a vow to Jehovah and pay it.

18142.label: Isaiah 19:22
18142.text: Jehovah will strike Egypt, striking and healing it; and they will return to Jehovah, and he will respond to their entreaties and heal them.

18143.label: Isaiah 19:23
18143.text: In that day there will be a highway out of Egypt to As·syrʹi·a. Then As·syrʹi·a will come into Egypt, and Egypt into As·syrʹi·a, and Egypt will serve God together with As·syrʹi·a.

18144.label: Isaiah 19:24
18144.text: In that day Israel will be the third along with Egypt and with As·syrʹi·a, a blessing in the midst of the earth,

18145.label: Isaiah 19:25
18145.text: for Jehovah of armies will have blessed it, saying: “Blessed be my people, Egypt, and the work of my hands, As·syrʹi·a, and my inheritance, Israel.”

18146.label: Isaiah 20:1
18146.text: In the year that King Sarʹgon of As·syrʹi·a sent the Tarʹtan to Ashʹdod, he fought against Ashʹdod and captured it.

18147.label: Isaiah 20:2
18147.text: At that time Jehovah spoke through Isaiah the son of Aʹmoz, saying: “Go, remove the sackcloth from your hips, and take your sandals off your feet.” And he did so, walking about naked and barefoot.

18148.label: Isaiah 20:3
18148.text: Jehovah then said: “Just as my servant Isaiah has walked about naked and barefoot for three years as a sign and a portent against Egypt and E·thi·oʹpi·a,

18149.label: Isaiah 20:4
18149.text: so the king of As·syrʹi·a will lead the captives of Egypt and the exiles of E·thi·oʹpi·a, boys and old men, naked and barefoot and with exposed buttocks, the nakedness of Egypt.

18150.label: Isaiah 20:5
18150.text: And they will be terrified and will be ashamed of E·thi·oʹpi·a their hope and of Egypt their pride.

18151.label: Isaiah 20:6
18151.text: The inhabitants of this coastland will say in that day, ‘Look at what happened to our hope, to which we fled for help and rescue from the king of As·syrʹi·a! How will we escape now?’”

18152.label: Isaiah 21:1
18152.text: A pronouncement against the wilderness of the sea: It is coming like storm winds that sweep through in the south,From the wilderness, from a fearsome land.

18153.label: Isaiah 21:2
18153.text: A harsh vision has been told to me: The treacherous one is acting treacherously,And the destroyer is destroying. Go up, O Eʹlam! Lay siege, O Meʹdi·a! I will put an end to all the sighing she caused.

18154.label: Isaiah 21:3
18154.text: That is why I am in great anguish. Convulsions have seized me,Like those of a woman giving birth. I am too distressed to hear;I am too disturbed to see.

18155.label: Isaiah 21:4
18155.text: My heart falters; I shudder in terror. The twilight I longed for makes me tremble.

18156.label: Isaiah 21:5
18156.text: Set the table and arrange the seats! Eat and drink! Get up, you princes, anoint the shield!

18157.label: Isaiah 21:6
18157.text: For this is what Jehovah said to me: “Go, post a lookout and have him report what he sees.”

18158.label: Isaiah 21:7
18158.text: And he saw a war chariot with a team of horses,A war chariot of donkeys,A war chariot of camels. He watched carefully, with great attentiveness.

18159.label: Isaiah 21:8
18159.text: Then he called out like a lion: “Upon the watchtower, O Jehovah, I am standing constantly by day,And I am stationed at my guardpost every night.

18160.label: Isaiah 21:9
18160.text: Look at what is coming: Men in a war chariot with a team of horses!” Then he spoke up and said: “She has fallen! Babylon has fallen! All the graven images of her gods he has shattered to the ground!”

18161.label: Isaiah 21:10
18161.text: O my people who have been threshed,The product of my threshing floor, I have reported to you what I have heard from Jehovah of armies, the God of Israel.

18162.label: Isaiah 21:11
18162.text: A pronouncement against Duʹmah: Someone is calling out to me from Seʹir: “Watchman, what of the night? Watchman, what of the night?”

18163.label: Isaiah 21:12
18163.text: The watchman said: “The morning is coming, and also the night. If you would inquire, inquire. Come again!”

18164.label: Isaiah 21:13
18164.text: A pronouncement against the desert plain: In the forest in the desert plain you will spend the night,O caravans of Deʹdan.

18165.label: Isaiah 21:14
18165.text: Bring water to meet the thirsty one,You inhabitants of the land of Teʹma, And bring bread for the one fleeing.

18166.label: Isaiah 21:15
18166.text: For they have fled from the swords, from the drawn sword,From the bent bow, and from the cruelty of the war.

18167.label: Isaiah 21:16
18167.text: For this is what Jehovah said to me: “Within one year, like the years of a hired worker, all the glory of Keʹdar will come to an end.

18168.label: Isaiah 21:17
18168.text: The remaining bowmen of the warriors of Keʹdar will be few, for Jehovah the God of Israel has spoken.”

18169.label: Isaiah 22:1
18169.text: A pronouncement about the Valley of Vision: What is the matter with you that you have all gone up to the roofs?

18170.label: Isaiah 22:2
18170.text: You were full of turmoil,A boisterous city, an exultant town. Your slain were not slain with the sword,Nor did they die in battle.

18171.label: Isaiah 22:3
18171.text: All your dictators have fled together. They were taken prisoner without need of a bow. All who were found were taken prisoner, Even though they had fled far away.

18172.label: Isaiah 22:4
18172.text: That is why I said: “Turn your eyes away from me,And I will weep bitterly. Do not insist on comforting meOver the destruction of the daughter of my people.

18173.label: Isaiah 22:5
18173.text: For it is a day of confusion and of defeat and of panic, From the Sovereign Lord, Jehovah of armies,In the Valley of Vision. There is a demolishing of the wall And a cry to the mountain.

18174.label: Isaiah 22:6
18174.text: Eʹlam picks up the quiverWith manned chariots and horses, And Kir uncovers the shield.

18175.label: Isaiah 22:7
18175.text: Your choicest valleys Will become full of war chariots,And the horses will take their positions at the gate,

18176.label: Isaiah 22:8
18176.text: And the screen of Judah will be removed. “In that day you will look toward the armory of the House of the Forest,

18177.label: Isaiah 22:9
18177.text: and you will see the many breaches of the City of David. And you will collect the waters of the lower pool.

18178.label: Isaiah 22:10
18178.text: You will count the houses of Jerusalem, and you will pull down the houses to reinforce the wall.

18179.label: Isaiah 22:11
18179.text: And you will make a basin between the two walls for the water of the old pool, but you will not look to its Grand Maker, and you will not see the One who formed it long ago.

18180.label: Isaiah 22:12
18180.text: In that day the Sovereign Lord, Jehovah of armies,Will call for weeping and mourning, For shaved heads and the wearing of sackcloth.

18181.label: Isaiah 22:13
18181.text: But instead, there is celebration and rejoicing,The killing of cattle and the slaughtering of sheep,The eating of meat and the drinking of wine. ‘Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we will die.’”

18182.label: Isaiah 22:14
18182.text: Then Jehovah of armies revealed himself in my ears: “‘This error will not be atoned in your behalf until you people die,’ says the Sovereign Lord, Jehovah of armies.”

18183.label: Isaiah 22:15
18183.text: This is what the Sovereign Lord, Jehovah of armies, says: “Go in to this steward, to Shebʹna, who is in charge of the house, and say,

18184.label: Isaiah 22:16
18184.text: ‘What is your interest here, and who is there of interest to you here, that you hewed out a burial place here for yourself?’ He is hewing out his burial place in a high place; he is cutting out a resting-place for himself in a crag.

18185.label: Isaiah 22:17
18185.text: ‘Look! Jehovah will hurl you down violently, O man, and seize you forcibly.

18186.label: Isaiah 22:18
18186.text: He will certainly wrap you up tightly and hurl you like a ball into a wide land. There you will die, and there your glorious chariots will be, a disgrace to your master’s house.

18187.label: Isaiah 22:19
18187.text: And I will depose you from your position and throw you out of your office.

18188.label: Isaiah 22:20
18188.text: “‘In that day I will call my servant E·liʹa·kim the son of Hil·kiʹah,

18189.label: Isaiah 22:21
18189.text: and I will clothe him with your robe and firmly bind your sash around him, and I will give your authority into his hand. And he will be a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem and to the house of Judah.

18190.label: Isaiah 22:22
18190.text: And I will put the key of the house of David on his shoulder. He will open and no one will shut; and he will shut and no one will open.

18191.label: Isaiah 22:23
18191.text: I will drive him in as a peg in a lasting place, and he will become as a throne of glory to the house of his father.

18192.label: Isaiah 22:24
18192.text: And they will hang on him all the glory of the house of his father, the descendants and the offspring, all the small vessels, the bowl-shaped vessels, as well as all the large jars.

18193.label: Isaiah 22:25
18193.text: “‘In that day,’ declares Jehovah of armies, ‘the peg that is driven in a lasting place will be removed, and it will be cut down and fall, and the load that it supported will fall to ruin, for Jehovah himself has spoken.’”

18194.label: Isaiah 23:1
18194.text: A pronouncement about Tyre: Wail, you ships of Tarʹshish! For the port has been destroyed; it cannot be entered. From the land of Kitʹtim it has been revealed to them.

18195.label: Isaiah 23:2
18195.text: Be silent, you inhabitants of the coastland. The merchants from Siʹdon who cross the sea have filled you.

18196.label: Isaiah 23:3
18196.text: Over many waters went the grain of Shiʹhor, The harvest of the Nile, her revenue,Bringing the profit of the nations.

18197.label: Isaiah 23:4
18197.text: Be ashamed, O Siʹdon, you stronghold of the sea,Because the sea has said: “I have not had birth pains, and I have not given birth,Nor have I brought up young men or raised young women.”

18198.label: Isaiah 23:5
18198.text: As when they heard the report about Egypt, People will be in anguish over the report about Tyre.

18199.label: Isaiah 23:6
18199.text: Cross over to Tarʹshish! Wail, you inhabitants of the coastland!

18200.label: Isaiah 23:7
18200.text: Is this your city that was exultant from long ago, from her early times? Her feet used to take her to distant lands to reside.

18201.label: Isaiah 23:8
18201.text: Who has decided this against Tyre,The bestower of crowns,Whose merchants were princes,Whose tradesmen were honored in all the earth?

18202.label: Isaiah 23:9
18202.text: Jehovah of armies himself has decided this,To profane her pride over all her beauty,To humiliate all those who were honored throughout the earth.

18203.label: Isaiah 23:10
18203.text: Cross over your land like the Nile River, O daughter of Tarʹshish. There is no longer any shipyard.

18204.label: Isaiah 23:11
18204.text: He has stretched his hand out over the sea;He has shaken kingdoms. Jehovah has ordered the annihilation of Phoe·niʹcia’s strongholds.

18205.label: Isaiah 23:12
18205.text: And he says: “You will exult no more, O oppressed one, the virgin daughter of Siʹdon. Get up, cross over to Kitʹtim. Even there you will find no rest.”

18206.label: Isaiah 23:13
18206.text: Look! The land of the Chal·deʹans. This is the people—As·syrʹi·a was not the one—They made her a place for those haunting the desert. They have erected their siege towers;They have stripped bare her fortified towers, Reducing her to a crumbling ruin.

18207.label: Isaiah 23:14
18207.text: Wail, you ships of Tarʹshish,For your stronghold has been destroyed.

18208.label: Isaiah 23:15
18208.text: In that day Tyre will be forgotten for 70 years, the same as the lifetime of one king. At the end of 70 years, it will happen to Tyre as in the song of a prostitute:

18209.label: Isaiah 23:16
18209.text: “Take a harp, go around the city, O forgotten prostitute. Play your harp skillfully;Sing many songs,So that they will remember you.”

18210.label: Isaiah 23:17
18210.text: At the end of 70 years, Jehovah will turn his attention to Tyre, and she will return to her hire and prostitute herself with all the world’s kingdoms on the face of the earth.

18211.label: Isaiah 23:18
18211.text: But her profit and her hire will become something holy to Jehovah. It will not be stored or laid away, because her hire will be for those dwelling before Jehovah, so that they may eat to satisfaction and wear elegant clothing.

18212.label: Isaiah 24:1
18212.text: Look! Jehovah is emptying the land and making it desolate. He turns it upside down and scatters its inhabitants.

18213.label: Isaiah 24:2
18213.text: It will be the same for everyone: The people as well as the priest,The servant and his master,The servant and her mistress,The buyer and the seller,The lender and the borrower,The creditor and the debtor.

18214.label: Isaiah 24:3
18214.text: The land will be completely emptied;It will be completely plundered, For Jehovah has spoken this word.

18215.label: Isaiah 24:4
18215.text: The land mourns; it is wasting away. The productive land withers; it is fading away. The prominent people of the land wither.

18216.label: Isaiah 24:5
